newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen rolling higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen rolling higher at open.

text.p: * Toronto stocks were expected to extend recent gains at Wednesday's open, as investors continue to pour money into the market. * Oils seen hot on higher crude prices.
Toronto's booming stock market was seen rolling higher at Wednesday's open on stronger banks, golds and oils and a continued lack of investment alternatives.

"I still think that Toronto is going to move to a new high," said one equities trader. Rising bonds prices should boost the influential financial services sector while firmer gold and crude oil prices could help heavyweight golds and oils, traders said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 8.86 points on Tuesday to 6801.17, its 29th record close this year.

A second trader added that despite concerns that North American stock markets are peaking and could soon suffer corrections, investors have few alternatives as bond prices are at all-time highs as well. "There's nowhere to go with the money."
Market analysts will be watching for more U.S. and Canadian economic indicators this week, including Friday's employment figures out of the U.S. for July.

* Laidlaw Inc LDM.TO, North America's largest school busing and emergency transportation company with healthcare interests, continued its acquisitive ways. It said on Wednesday that it snapped up Dallas, Tex.-based, physician services management firm Emcare Holdings Inc for $400 million cash or $38 a share.
* Intergrated energy firm Petro-Canada Inc was upgraded to outperform from neutral by brokerage Morgan Stanley.
* Canada's air carriers, Canadian Airlines Corp and Air Canada, are expected to post second quarter earnings soon.
